title: Evaluation of medical imaging devices using synthetically modified clinical images and 3D printed phantoms
eli5: Hospital scanners give numbers that doctors use to pick treatments. But how do we know those numbers are right? I built pretend tumours: some printed in 3D plastic, some drawn by a computer inside real scans. Because I made them, I know the right answer, so I can check whether the scanner tells the truth.
abstractShort: A hybrid framework combining 3D-printed phantoms with synthetic lesion insertion into raw PET data, giving a ground truth that is physically anchored, can represent spatial heterogeneity, and scales to datasets for AI and radiomics.

chapters.title: The problem
chapters.detail: Clinical trials lack ground truth; standard phantoms only have uniform spheres; simulations are models, not reality.

chapters.title: Sponges that set the brightness
chapters.eli5: Holes in a printed cube decide how bright it glows.
chapters.detail: Porosity encodes contrast (solidity 50–75 % → TBR 2.0–4.0). 36-cube phantom on GE DMI: designed contrast held; preparation drove day-to-day change.

more.question: Do porous inserts keep their quantitative response across repeated preparations and acquisitions?

figures.caption: From a solid cube to a porous lattice: the printed geometry sets how much tracer each insert holds.
PET of the four phantom layers across five preparation days.

methods: 36-insert phantom (40 mm cubes in an S–Dp–T grid: solidity 50/60/70 %, pore distance 5/7/10 mm, targets 10/15/20 mm)
Repeated [18F]FDG acquisitions on a TOF 5-ring GE Discovery MI, Q.Clear (BSREM) with IUCT clinical settings
Metrics: SUV, target representation index (RC), dilution coefficient, HU; Friedman + Kendall W, Wilcoxon–Holm, MAPE, TOST ±10/15 %
results: Designed contrast stayed visible on every day
Dilution coefficients clustered around theory (e.g. 70 % solidity: 0.32–0.40 vs 0.30), mostly inside the 10 % margin
Only DCmax differed significantly across days (p = 0.03): preparation, not design, drove day-to-day change
CT attenuation drifted +1.5–2.7 HU/day as the print saturated with water
limitations: Manual VOIs; SUV used total rather than fillable phantom weight (fixed in later studies: 4.5–4.6 L)
Material and preparation protocol need standardising

chapters.title: The computer copies the cube
chapters.eli5: A computer-drawn cube looks just like the printed one.
chapters.detail: Synthetic insertion (DUETTO) reproduced mean contrast within about 0–6 %; peak values stayed biased.

more.question: Does synthetic lesion insertion reproduce the measured response of uniform printed targets?

figures.caption: Synthetic lesion insertion (DUETTO, left) versus the real acquisition (right) across three decay windows.

methods: One layer of the 36-insert phantom, [18F]FDG (58.7 MBq), 3 frames on the DMI
Synthetic insertion into raw PET data with GE DUETTO, then TOF-BSREM reconstruction
Visual comparison plus mean and peak recovery, ±10 % MAPE bounds
results: No major visual difference between synthetic and acquired targets
Mean contrast matched within 0–6 % for 15 and 20 mm targets
Peak values stayed systematically higher in simulation (≈ 7–15 %)
limitations: Designed vs measured insert contrast needs calibrating; higher contrasts (10:1) untested

chapters.title: Same recipe, two hospitals
chapters.eli5: Email the design file and another hospital gets the same answer.
chapters.detail: Printed at two facilities from shared files, scanned on DMI and OMNI: met ±10 % equivalence bounds.

more.question: Do inserts printed at different hospitals from the same design files give the same answer?

figures.caption: Central PET slices of each layer at both facilities, on DMI and OMNI scanners.
Background SUV per layer for every facility, scanner and day stays within the ±10 % bound.

methods: Same 36-insert design printed independently at two facilities
Day 0 and day 8 on TOF DMI (5 × 300 s) and non-TOF OMNI Legend (5 × 420 s), EARL-style preparation, BSREM
HU, SUV, RC, DC and target-to-background ratio; same three-level statistical hierarchy
results: Homogeneous mixing confirmed: every layer comparison inside 10 % bounds
15 and 20 mm targets within 10 % of the designed TBR at both sites
Only 2–3 of 54 RC/TBR values exceeded 10 % MAPE
CT-based attenuation maps contributed equally at both sites
limitations: Nominal ROIs don't capture print geometry errors; next: more sites, vendors and a NEMA reference

chapters.title: Tumours with patterns inside
chapters.eli5: Real tumours are patchy, so the printed ones are patchy too.
chapters.detail: Nested necrosis-like inserts, [18F]FDG and [68Ga]PSMA. Gini index as physical heterogeneity truth; radiomic rank agreement ρ 0.76–0.92. CASSOULET reproduced the trends.

more.question: Can printed multi-uptake inserts be told apart and ranked consistently, with two tracers and in simulation?

figures.caption: Nine heterogeneous insert designs at three sizes, scanned with [18F]FDG and [68Ga]PSMA.
The same inserts: physical phantom versus CASSOULET simulation.
Gini index of heterogeneity: theory, FDG and Ga-68 follow the same trend.

methods: 27 inserts, 9 nested patterns (incipient → full necrosis) at 17, 22 and 28 mm, peak TBR 4:1
[18F]FDG and [68Ga]PSMA on the OMNI Legend at 50 and 30 MBq
Gini index as a physical measure of heterogeneity; 60 radiomic features (IBSI families)
CASSOULET: simulated OMNI model, OSEM 2×10 with PSF, 5 mm smoothing
results: Designed patterns separable by first- and second-order metrics
Cross-tracer rank agreement: median ρ 0.76–0.92 (GLRLM strongest)
Gini trends matched between tracers and between experiment and simulation
Simulation reproduced trends more reliably than absolute texture values (median feature error 18–31 %)
limitations: BSREM (experiment) vs OSEM (simulation) noise texture differs; 30 MBq count matching needs tuning

chapters.title: Real tumour shapes, twice
chapters.eli5: Copy real tumour shapes, print them, and also hide them in a healthy scan.
chapters.detail: 8 TCIA lesion geometries, printed and inserted into healthy-volunteer total-body PET. Dice 0.67–0.92, cross-domain difference 0.04 ± 0.03.

more.question: Can the same patient-derived lesion be realised both as a printed insert and as a synthetic lesion in a clinical background?

figures.caption: The hybrid workflow: segmented clinical lesions become both 3D-printed inserts and synthetic insertions.
Metabolic tumour volume for each lesion: source geometry, phantom and simulation.

methods: Eight TCIA-derived lesion geometries (5.9–23.6 mL, 40–66 mm), TBR 3:1–5:1
Physical: porous PLA inserts in a Jaszczak phantom, 100 MBq [18F]FDG, OMNI Legend, BSREM
Synthetic: inserted into healthy-volunteer total-body [18F]FDG PET via an OMNI-like forward projection and OSEM
MTV (42 % max and peak), Dice, Jaccard, TBR, CRC, CoV, TLG
results: Threshold MTVs exceeded source volumes in both domains (×1.3–2.3)
Lesion-specific trends in TBR, contrast recovery and CoV preserved across domains
limitations: Proof of concept: tests consistent behaviour, not absolute interchangeability
Healthy-volunteer data from a different scanner (Quadra) resampled to the OMNI geometry

takeaway: Toward ground-truth tools that are physically anchored, anatomically realistic, and scalable for AI.
